summary: Help 5–7 year-olds hold a few vivid, accurate polar-bear facts: polar bears live only in the Arctic (the far North, never with Antarctic penguins); they stay warm with BOTH thick fur AND a layer of fat (blubber) that trap the bear's own warmth rather than making heat; their fur only looks white while the skin beneath is black; they are strong swimmers; and they hunt seals by waiting patiently at breathing holes in the sea ice. A picture-first, explore-and-reveal approach suits this age, with a behaviour mini-scene and a true/false check as supports.
misconceptions: Polar bears and penguins live together — polar bears are Arctic (north) only; penguins are in the south
Polar bears are white all the way through — the fur only looks white and the skin beneath is black
They stay warm with fur alone — they also have a thick layer of fat (blubber)
Polar bears can't swim — they are strong swimmers who cross open water
They catch seals by chasing them — they mostly wait patiently at holes in the sea ice

activities.title: Explore a labelled polar bear on the sea ice
steps: Look at a labelled picture of a polar bear standing on Arctic sea ice, and point to or tap each part to reveal one fact.
Reveal the coat: 'thick fur traps the bear's own warmth, like a thick coat.'

Open a cutaway of the fur to find TWO things underneath — a layer of fat (blubber) and, surprisingly, black skin. The main way the bear stays warm is the fur plus the blubber working together; alongside that, the dark skin is thought to help soak up a little warmth from the Sun, and the fur only looks white.
Reveal the big paws to see the bear swimming strongly across open water.
Reveal a dark hole in the ice to watch the bear wait patiently beside it until a seal's nose appears.
Lift a flap answering 'Would a polar bear ever meet a penguin?' — the bear maps firmly to the far North, wild penguins to the southern half of the world, so in the wild the answer is never.
activities.insight: A polar bear is built for the Arctic: it keeps warm mainly with thick fur on top of black skin, with a layer of blubber underneath the skin, swims strongly, and depends on the sea ice to hunt seals — and in the wild it never shares a home with penguins.

activities.title: Act out the patient ice-hole hunt and the warm layers
steps: Play the bear waiting silently and still beside a hole in the ice until a seal surfaces — notice the bear mostly waits rather than chases.
Build the warm layers by placing or dragging 'fur' on the outside and 'fat (blubber)' on the inside of a bear outline, like putting a coat over a jumper.
Say aloud what each layer does: it keeps the bear's warmth in and the cold out.
activities.insight: Staying warm comes from two trapping layers working together, and a key way polar bears hunt seals is by waiting patiently at breathing holes in the ice rather than chasing — both make the bear's dependence on the sea ice felt.

activities.title: Fix the friend's facts: diagnostic check
steps: Listen to a friend's claim: 'Polar bears live at both the North and the South Pole, and their fur is white because their skin is white underneath — that's what keeps them warm.'
Say what you would fix in what the friend said.
Explain how a polar bear ACTUALLY keeps warm.
activities.insight: A secure understanding restricts polar bears to the Arctic, corrects the skin to black (fur only looks white), and names fur PLUS blubber as insulation that traps warmth — not skin colour.

checkQuestion: Here is a polar bear on the sea ice. A friend says 'polar bears live at both the North and the South Pole, and their fur is white because their skin is white underneath — that's what keeps them warm.' What would you fix in what your friend said, and how does a polar bear ACTUALLY keep warm?
checkAnswer: Two fixes: polar bears live ONLY in the Arctic (the North), never near the penguins in the Antarctic; and their skin is actually BLACK, not white — the fur only looks white. They keep warm with two things: a thick coat of fur AND a thick layer of fat called blubber under the skin. They are also strong swimmers and hunt seals by waiting at breathing holes in the ice.
